short_definition: A plug-and-play Data Engineering and Governance practice for Microsoft Fabric.
long_definition: A plug-and-play Data Engineering and Governance practice for Microsoft Fabric, implemented through a planned operating workflow, standardized notebook templates, reusable notebook-facing functions, and a shared metadata model.
preferred_usage: Use as the public project name.
avoid_usage: full data product platform

short_definition: A summary of the data at a point in time.
long_definition: A Profile is a summary of the data at a point in time. It shows things like row count, columns, data types, nulls, distinct values, minimum and maximum values, and value distributions. In FabricOps, this is stored in Data Profiled and Data Profiled Frequency metadata.
preferred_usage: Use profile for a summary of the data at a point in time.
avoid_usage: profile evidence; catalogue evidence

short_definition: Business and governance information added to the Data Catalogue after technical metadata has been captured.
long_definition: Enrichment is the business and governance information added to the Data Catalogue after the technical metadata has been captured. It includes descriptions, ownership, sensitivity, classification, and how the data is intended to be used.
preferred_usage: Use enrichment for business and governance information added to the Data Catalogue.
avoid_usage: metadata enrichment when enrichment is sufficient

short_definition: Governed rules FabricOps applies to data and pipelines.
long_definition: Guardrails are the governed rules FabricOps applies to data and pipelines. Today, they can check schema, freshness, profile behaviour, change over time, and data quality. In future they can also cover governance requirements such as stricter handling for sensitive data, masking or restricted access for PII, and additional controls for specific classifications.
preferred_usage: Use guardrails for governed rules applied to data and pipelines; use singular only for grammar.
avoid_usage: guardrail governance

short_definition: Applying active Guardrails during a pipeline run and acting on the result.
long_definition: Enforcement is when FabricOps applies the active Guardrails during a pipeline run and acts on the result. Depending on the Guardrail, the pipeline can continue, continue with a warning, or stop.
preferred_usage: Use enforcement for applying active Guardrails during execution.
avoid_usage: runtime enforcement when enforcement is sufficient

short_definition: The recorded outcome after FabricOps evaluates a Guardrail during a pipeline run.
long_definition: A Guardrail Result is the recorded outcome after FabricOps evaluates a Guardrail during a pipeline run. It records whether the check passed, warned, or failed, what was checked, and whether the pipeline is allowed to continue.
preferred_usage: Use guardrail result for what happened when FabricOps applied a Guardrail.
avoid_usage: rule result

short_definition: The person or role responsible for reviewing and maintaining the governance context for data.
long_definition: A Data Steward is the person or role responsible for reviewing and maintaining the governance context for data, including its meaning, ownership, sensitivity, intended use, and governance decisions.
preferred_usage: Use data steward for the accountable governance role in FabricOps.
avoid_usage: owner when stewardship is meant

short_definition: The governed record that establishes who is sharing what data, with whom, and why.
long_definition: A Data Agreement establishes the governed context for a dataset before engineering proceeds. It captures the parties involved, steward context, intended use, and expectations that guide the FabricOps workflow.
preferred_usage: Use data agreement for the governed agreement that starts the FabricOps workflow.
avoid_usage: data contract when the earlier agreement stage is meant

short_definition: The approved definition of what is expected from governed Production data.
long_definition: A Data Contract is the approved definition of the structure, meaning, quality expectations, ownership, processing expectations, and governance requirements for governed Production data.
preferred_usage: Use data contract for the approved Production-facing contract.
avoid_usage: data agreement when the approved Production contract is meant

short_definition: Information about the data.
long_definition: Metadata is information about the data. In FabricOps this includes its structure, Profile, ownership, business meaning, sensitivity, Guardrails, lineage, Data Agreement, Data Contract, and other information used to understand and govern it.
preferred_usage: Use metadata for information that describes or governs data.
avoid_usage: evidence or context when the specific metadata can be named

short_definition: Controlling repeatable engineering behaviour through configuration instead of rewriting pipeline code.
long_definition: Configuration-driven Engineering means defining reusable pipeline behaviour through configuration so teams can change settings, targets, strategies, and governed parameters without duplicating or rewriting the underlying engineering logic.
preferred_usage: Use configuration-driven engineering for engineering behaviour controlled by configuration.
avoid_usage: hard-coded engineering when configuration is the intended control

short_definition: Defining governance rules in a structured, version-controlled form that can be applied consistently.
long_definition: Governance as Code means defining governance rules in a structured, version-controlled way so they can be reviewed, repeated, and applied consistently by FabricOps. This can include Guardrails, data quality rules, sensitivity and PII requirements, access rules, approvals, governance states, and other policies that can be expressed as configuration or executable checks.
preferred_usage: Use governance as code as the umbrella term; treat policy as code as an alias within this concept.
avoid_usage: policy as code as a separate FabricOps concept

short_definition: The governed definition of who is allowed to access data and under what conditions.
long_definition: Data Access describes who is allowed to access governed data and the conditions or restrictions that apply. It provides the governance context that can be implemented through platform security controls such as RLS, OLS, permissions, or other access mechanisms.
preferred_usage: Use data access for the governed access requirement, not a specific technical security implementation.
avoid_usage: RLS or OLS when the broader access requirement is meant

short_definition: How carefully data should be handled based on its confidentiality or risk.
long_definition: Data Sensitivity describes how carefully data should be handled based on confidentiality, privacy, business risk, or regulatory requirements. It can influence access, masking, sharing, and other governance controls.
preferred_usage: Use data sensitivity for the handling classification of governed data.
avoid_usage: PII when the broader sensitivity concept is meant

short_definition: Data that can identify or be linked to an individual.
long_definition: PII, or personally identifiable information, is data that can identify or be linked to an individual. In a governed workflow it may require additional controls such as restricted access, masking, or stricter handling.
preferred_usage: Use PII after personally identifiable information is clear from context.
avoid_usage: sensitive data when specifically referring to personal identifiers

short_definition: Microsoft's analytics platform used as the runtime for FabricOps.
long_definition: Microsoft Fabric is the analytics platform FabricOps runs on, providing workspaces, Lakehouses, Warehouses, notebooks, Spark, SQL, and other data capabilities.
preferred_usage: Use the full product name on first mention.
avoid_usage: Fabric alone when ambiguous

short_definition: A Microsoft Fabric container for related data and analytics items.
long_definition: A Workspace is a Microsoft Fabric container used to organize and secure related items such as notebooks, Lakehouses, Warehouses, semantic models, and reports.
preferred_usage: Use workspace for the Fabric organizational and security boundary.
avoid_usage: tenant

short_definition: A Fabric data store that combines data-lake storage with managed tables for analytics and Spark workloads.
long_definition: A Lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric stores files and managed Delta tables in OneLake and is commonly used with Spark, notebooks, and SQL analytics endpoints.
preferred_usage: Use Lakehouse for the Microsoft Fabric item type.
avoid_usage: lake house

short_definition: A Fabric relational data store designed for SQL analytics and warehousing workloads.
long_definition: A Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric provides relational tables and SQL-based querying for structured analytics and data warehousing workloads.
preferred_usage: Use Warehouse for the Microsoft Fabric item type.
avoid_usage: SQL database when Fabric Warehouse is meant

short_definition: An interactive Fabric document for running code, data processing, analysis, and engineering workflows.
long_definition: A Notebook is an interactive Microsoft Fabric document where users can run Python, PySpark, SQL, and other supported code for data engineering, analysis, experimentation, and operational workflows.
preferred_usage: Use notebook for the Fabric notebook users work in.
avoid_usage: Jupyter notebook when the Fabric runtime matters

short_definition: A sequence of steps that moves, transforms, checks, and writes data.
long_definition: A Pipeline is a repeatable sequence of data-processing steps that can read source data, transform it, apply checks, and write results to a target.
preferred_usage: Use pipeline for an end-to-end data-processing flow.
avoid_usage: workflow when a data pipeline is specifically meant

short_definition: The Python API for Apache Spark.
long_definition: PySpark lets Python code use Apache Spark to process data across a distributed compute engine. It is commonly used in Fabric notebooks for large-scale transformations and data engineering.
preferred_usage: Use PySpark when referring to Python code running on Spark.
avoid_usage: Python when Spark execution is the important distinction

short_definition: Processing multiple parts of a workload at the same time.
long_definition: Parallel Processing divides work so multiple tasks or data partitions can be processed at the same time, which can reduce elapsed processing time when the workload and compute resources support it.
preferred_usage: Use parallel processing for concurrent work across tasks, partitions, or workers.
avoid_usage: multithreading when the broader distributed-processing concept is meant

short_definition: Patterns for handling changes to descriptive records over time.
long_definition: Slowly Changing Dimensions are data-modelling patterns for handling changes to descriptive records. Common approaches include SCD Type 1, which replaces the previous value, and SCD Type 2, which keeps history by creating versioned records.
preferred_usage: Use slowly changing dimensions when discussing SCD patterns; introduce SCD before using the abbreviation alone.
avoid_usage: incremental load when the history-management pattern is meant

short_definition: Organizing data structures and relationships so data can be stored, understood, and used effectively.
long_definition: Data Modelling is the practice of designing tables, fields, keys, relationships, and structures so data supports its intended analytical, operational, or reporting use.
preferred_usage: Use data modelling for the design of data structures and relationships.
avoid_usage: schema when the broader model design is meant

short_definition: The defined structure of data, including its columns and data types.
long_definition: A Schema describes the structure of a dataset or table, including column names, data types, and other structural expectations.
preferred_usage: Use schema for the defined structure of data.
avoid_usage: layout when schema is meant

short_definition: Whether data meets the expectations required for its intended use.
long_definition: Data Quality describes whether data meets expected rules for things such as completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, accuracy, and other requirements needed for its intended use.
preferred_usage: Use data quality in narrative text; use DQ after the meaning is established.
avoid_usage: quality alone when data quality is meant

short_definition: A write strategy that adds new rows without replacing existing rows.
long_definition: Append adds new rows to an existing target while leaving existing rows unchanged. It is appropriate only when incoming data is additive and existing records do not need to be changed or removed.
preferred_usage: Use append for the additive target write strategy.
avoid_usage: incremental load when the read scope rather than write strategy is meant

short_definition: A write strategy that replaces existing target data.
long_definition: Overwrite replaces existing target data with the newly prepared data. Depending on the implementation, it can replace a whole table or only a governed partition scope.
preferred_usage: Use overwrite for the replacement target write strategy.
avoid_usage: SCD Type 1 when record-level matching and updates are meant

short_definition: A security method that controls which rows of data a user can see.
long_definition: Row-Level Security limits the rows returned to a user based on identity, role, or access rules while allowing the same table or model to serve different audiences.
preferred_usage: Use row-level security on first mention; use RLS after it is established.
avoid_usage: role-level security

short_definition: A security method that controls whether a user can see specific tables or columns.
long_definition: Object-Level Security restricts access to specific data objects, such as tables or columns, so unauthorized users cannot see those objects even when they can access the wider model or dataset.
preferred_usage: Use object-level security on first mention; use OLS after it is established.
avoid_usage: row-level security when the restriction applies to tables or columns

short_definition: The rules and mechanisms that determine who can access data or system resources.
long_definition: Access Control is the broader set of rules and mechanisms used to decide who can access datasets, tables, columns, workspaces, files, or other resources and what actions they are allowed to perform.
preferred_usage: Use access control for the broad security concept; use RLS or OLS when a specific mechanism is meant.
avoid_usage: data access when discussing the technical enforcement mechanism rather than the governed requirement

short_definition: Settings that define how FabricOps or a pipeline should behave without changing the underlying code.
long_definition: Configuration is the set of named settings used to control environment targets, processing choices, rules, parameters, and other behaviour without rewriting the implementation.
preferred_usage: Use configuration in narrative text; use config in code-oriented shorthand.
avoid_usage: hard-coded values when behaviour should be configurable

short_definition: A source processing strategy that reads the complete physical source dataset for every run.
long_definition: A source processing strategy that reads the complete physical source dataset for every run.
preferred_usage: Use full dataset when a complete source read is intended.
avoid_usage: full load when the source strategy is meant

short_definition: A source processing strategy that uses a checkpoint column to process rows newer than the last successfully committed watermark.
long_definition: A source processing strategy that uses a checkpoint column to process rows newer than the last successfully committed watermark.
preferred_usage: Use incremental watermark for row-level ranges based on a reliable checkpoint column.
avoid_usage: incremental without explaining how changes are identified

short_definition: A source processing strategy that processes whole logical data buckets, such as days, months, or snapshots, when those buckets are new or changed.
long_definition: A source processing strategy that processes whole logical data buckets, such as days, months, or snapshots, when those buckets are new or changed.
preferred_usage: Use incremental partition for logical source buckets that can be processed or reprocessed as a whole.
avoid_usage: physical partitioning

short_definition: The runtime read mode used when FabricOps determines that only part of the source needs to be processed for the current run.
long_definition: The runtime read mode used when FabricOps determines that only part of the source needs to be processed for the current run.
preferred_usage: Use incremental subset only for the resolved runtime read mode.
avoid_usage: incremental diff

short_definition: A checkpoint value that records how far a successful incremental source load has processed.
long_definition: A checkpoint value that records how far a successful incremental source load has processed.
preferred_usage: Use watermark for the last successfully committed checkpoint value.
avoid_usage: source observation

short_definition: A logical data bucket such as a day, month, or snapshot that can be processed or reprocessed as a whole.
long_definition: A logical data bucket such as a day, month, or snapshot that can be processed or reprocessed as a whole.
preferred_usage: Use partition for the logical bucket in incremental partition source processing.
avoid_usage: physical partition when logical processing is meant

short_definition: How a Lakehouse table is physically organized for storage and pruning. This is separate from FabricOps incremental partition source processing.
long_definition: How a Lakehouse table is physically organized for storage and pruning. This is separate from FabricOps incremental partition source processing.
preferred_usage: Use physical partitioning when describing Lakehouse storage layout.
avoid_usage: incremental partition
